report.source_text: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination showed a protein level of 0.74 g/L with a glucose of 3.2 mmol/L (serum 5.5 mmol/L), <1 white blood cell per millilitre and negative oligoclonal bands. CSF PCR for viruses including JC and HIV were also negative. CSF cytology showed a moderately cellular fluid with increased numbers of lymphocytes and macrophages with no atypical cells, consistent with a mild chronic inflammatory/reactive process.

report.source_text: Treatment commenced, including high-dose methotrexate, cytarabine and rituximab, followed by radiotherapy (40 Gy total). Repeat MRI showed significant improvement in the central nervous system disease (figure 1G–I) and she also improved functionally, being discharged home without a package of care after previously needing 24 h nursing care. Ten months later, functional status had not deteriorated and neuropsychometric testing was equivalent to that done several months prior to commencement of treatment (ie, before significant further cognitive decline), however remaining below premorbid estimates. Importantly, her gait and mobility also improved dramatically as she went from being unable to walk unaided immediately prior to treatment, to walking independently, swimming twice weekly and using a cross-trainer regularly.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old woman presented with progressive personality change, emotional lability, and amnestic syndrome over 3 weeks, alongside language difficulties and apraxia. Neurological exam revealed brisk reflexes without clonus or extensor plantar responses. MRI brain showed diffuse confluent T2 hyperintensity without mass or contrast enhancement. CSF analysis showed mild chronic inflammation without atypical cells. Brain biopsy histology revealed diffuse and nodular infiltration by large atypical lymphoid cells with nuclear pleomorphism and perivascular clustering, confirming lymphoma. Bone marrow biopsy and PET/CT scans excluded systemic lymphoma. Treatment with high-dose methotrexate, cytarabine, rituximab, and radiotherapy led to significant clinical and radiological improvement with stable neuropsychometric testing at 10 months follow-up.

MRI brain demonstrated diffuse confluent T2 hyperintensity without mass effect or contrast enhancement (E005)
CSF analysis revealed mild inflammatory changes without atypical cells and negative viral studies (E007)
Brain biopsy histology showed diffuse and nodular infiltration by large atypical lymphoid cells with nuclear pleomorphism and perivascular clustering, indicating lymphoma (E011)
Bone marrow biopsy and PET/CT scan revealed no systemic lymphoma outside the CNS (E012)
Treatment with chemotherapy and radiotherapy resulted in marked improvement clinically and on MRI with stable neuropsychometric performance at 10 months follow-up (E013)
